messages:

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Verity is excited to move forward. Our legal team attached a marked-up DPA (Verity_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx) with a few items we'd like to resolve before signature:

- Confirm our right to audit (limited to SOC2 evidence + 30d notice)

I'm copying Maya (procurement) on timing. Can Redwood accept the redlines, or should we run a quick call with legal to walk through? Aim is to finish signature this month.

Best,
Luke Turner

Verity Health Systems

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Verity DPA - redlines attached

Neha / Karthik — forwarding Verity's redlines and SOC2 summary. High priority small healthcare prospect, deal id VER-2028-0432. Quick asks:

1) Can legal accept their limited audit wording (SOC2 evidence + 30d notice) or propose language?
2) Data residency: Verity wants explicit patient-data residency in us-east-1 — they may need an SCC carveout for EU patients; verify if we can commit to region-specific storage for HIPAA-scoped datasets.
3) Signer routing: procurement (Maya) prefers e-signature via DocuSign to Redwoods' standard exec route — they want CEO or Head of Legal signature. Suggest mapping: Procurement signs first, then Redwood legal + CEO final sign-off? Any concerns?

I'm available for a 30-min sync if easier.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachments: Verity_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx, Verity_SOC2_Summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Verity DPA - redlines attached

Thanks for the ping. Quick read-through — high level: we can accept most of the redlines but need to propose clarifying language rather than wholesale concessions. Specifics:

- Audit: Acceptable to limit to SOC2 report + 30 days notice, but add explicit scope/controls (e.g., "audit of controls relevant to the processing of Verity personal data; remote evidence preferred; in-person permitted only with prior mutual agreement and reimbursement").
- Data residency: We can commit to region-level storage for HIPAA-scoped patient records if they agree to a named-region addendum (us-east-1) and acknowledge it may require dedicated configuration and potential surcharge.
- De-identified datasets: propose explicit definition and allowed uses; Redwood will not re-identify or link datasets without a court order.

Signer flow: recommend standard: Procurement (Maya) countersigns first (DocuSign), Legal countersigns second, Exec (Head of Legal or COO) final signature only if there are non-standard indemnities or retention changes. That keeps velocity and avoids exec bottleneck.

I can draft a response and a concise redline (track-changes) to send back. Also suggest attaching SCCs_Export_List.xlsx for transparency on subprocessors/data flows.

-Karthik
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jan 2028 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Verity DPA - redlines attached

All,

I've drafted the suggested language and attached a short summary that addresses Verity's three asks. Key points to include in our reply:

- Audit: "Remote-first" SOC2 evidence clause, with an explicit escalation path if additional evidence is required (legal-to-legal). Limit frequency to once per 12 months.
- Residency: Agree to a named-region commitment for HIPAA-scoped data; include a surcharge clause and a 30-day lead time for configuration.
- De-id: Add an explicit definition and a prohibition on re-identification without a court order or written consent.

Routing/Execution: agree with Karthik's flow. I recommend we prepare two DocuSign envelopes:
1) Commercial + DPA as negotiated (Procurement signs)
2) Exec acceptance envelope (Legal + Exec) triggered only if the DPA deviates from our standard templates beyond these changes.

I'll attach the redline file (I converted it to our standard template) and the SCCs table for their review. Vanessa — if you can confirm whether Verity expects a fully executed contract by end of month, I'll prioritize the redline.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Verity_DPA_Redlines_Redwood_v1.docx, SCCs_Export_List.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Luke Turner <l.turner@verityhealth.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@verityhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Verity DPA - redlines attached

Luke / Maya,

Thanks for sending the redlines. Redwood legal reviewed and proposed narrow clarifications rather than broad changes; summary attached. High-level:

- Audit: We can accept SOC2 evidence + 30d notice with the remote-first approach Karthik described.
- Residency: We can commit to keeping HIPAA-scoped patient records in us-east-1 with a configuration lead time (30 days) and a nominal add-on to the subscription.
- De-identified datasets: We added an explicit definition and re-identification prohibition.

Next steps (to keep momentum):
1) Please confirm that DocuSign is acceptable for your side. If yes, we'll send the first envelope to Procurement (Maya) for countersign with the commercial terms + proposed DPA redlines.
2) If Procurement needs exec signature up-front, let us know and we'll adjust the envelopes per Karthik's routing suggestion.

When you confirm, I'll trigger the DocuSign link and share the HubSpot record. Goal: fully executed within 7 business days after your confirmation.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
